prompt.context: Your client, Silverado, is a manufacturer of silverware that is sold to households and restaurants. The company has been in the industry for over 80 years and has a very strong brand name. Silverado has experienced declining revenue growth for the past 5 years.
prompt.question: Silverado's CEO would like to understand why revenue growth has been declining and how the company can restore its previous high revenue growth rates.

clarifying_info.q: Is the issue on the revenue side or the cost side?
clarifying_info.a: The key to profitability is not associated with reducing costs — focus on the revenue side.
Silverado has been selling luxury silverware for many years. Five years ago, Silverado created a new division and started selling generic brand silverware.

clarifying_info.q: How has the overall market been growing?
clarifying_info.a: The market is mature; market growth will remain steady for the next few years. (Exhibit 1 will be provided.)

exhibits.title: Annual Revenues and Market Share 2007–2011
exhibits.shows: Bar chart and table showing annual revenues for Silverado and its competitors from 2007 to 2011, along with Silverado's annual growth rate each year.

exhibits.title: Revenue, Cost, and Units Sold by Product (2011)
exhibits.shows: Table showing price per unit, units sold, and COGS for luxury and generic product lines, plus historical units sold for each line from 2007 to 2011.

exhibits.title: Luxury Silverware Price Elasticity
exhibits.shows: Table showing quantity demanded (in thousands) at various price points for luxury silverware.

framework: Understand market dynamics: overall market size, growth trends, and Silverado's market share vs. competitors
Diagnose revenue drivers: break revenue into price × volume for each product segment (luxury vs. generic)
Assess competitive landscape: new entrants, pricing pressure, brand positioning
Evaluate operational constraints: manufacturing capacity, distribution channels
Identify growth levers: pricing strategy in luxury segment, generic segment outlook, new product tiers, M&A

questions.prompt: Question 1 — Looking at Exhibit 1, what are potential reasons Silverado's revenue growth is declining despite overall market growth?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate will quickly interpret the revenue and growth charts and list multiple hypotheses without prompting. Key hypotheses include: growth in the generic segment has slowed; manufacturing capacity cannot keep up with demand; increased competition is eroding market share; price competition is pressuring margins or volume; lack of distribution channels; inadequate marketing; Silverado is not competitive in a growing market segment.

questions.prompt: Question 2 — Please interpret the market and revenue/cost charts. What do you observe about the two product segments?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate gross margins for each segment and note the slowdown in generic unit growth. Key observations: (1) growth in the generic segment has slowed sharply; (2) luxury gross margin (~50%) is more than twice the generic gross margin (~20%). After the candidate responds, provide background info: several new competitors with massive overseas production have captured excess surplus demand in generic; Silverado's manufacturing capacity has not kept up with demand for generic products; research indicates it will take more than 2 years before Silverado can access overseas factories; other competitors are building brand recognition in the lower-end market.

math.setup: Calculate 2011 gross margin for each product line. Revenue = Price × Units. Gross margin = (Revenue − COGS) / Revenue.
math.answer: Luxury gross margin ≈ 50%; Generic gross margin ≈ 20%. Luxury margin is more than twice generic margin.

questions.prompt: Question 3 — Using the price elasticity data, what is the optimal price for luxury silverware and what revenue growth would the price change generate?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate total luxury revenue at each price point, identify the revenue-maximizing price ($240), compute the incremental revenue vs. the current baseline, and benchmark that growth rate against Silverado's historical growth to assess whether the price change alone restores prior growth. A superior candidate notes that $240 maximizes revenue but this alone will not restore peak growth rates.

math.setup: Calculate total luxury revenue at each price point (Price × Quantity). Current baseline: $150 × 180,000 = $27M. Total current revenue (2011) = $52M.
steps: Implied next-year growth rate (due to price change alone) = $9M / $52M ≈ 17%
Historical peak growth rates were ~26%, so the price change alone does not restore peak growth.
math.answer: Optimal price = $240; luxury revenue rises to $36M (+$9M). Growth rate from price change alone ≈ 17%, below historical peak of ~26%.

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the pricing lever, what other creative ideas could Silverado pursue to restore revenue growth?

categories.name: New product tiers
ideas: Introduce a middle-tier product line to capture the price gap between $25 generic and $150 luxury
Bundle silverware sets for wedding registries or corporate gifting

categories.name: Acquisitions
ideas: Acquire a competitor with overseas manufacturing capacity to accelerate generic growth
Acquire a complementary brand with established distribution in new geographies

categories.name: Distribution & channels
ideas: Expand into new retail channels (e-commerce, specialty kitchenware stores)
Partner with restaurant chains for bulk supply contracts

categories.name: Marketing & brand
ideas: Leverage 80-year brand heritage in luxury marketing campaigns
Develop brand loyalty programs to deepen retention in the luxury segment

categories.name: Operational improvements
ideas: Fast-track access to overseas factories to resolve capacity constraint for generic
License manufacturing to a third party as an interim capacity solution

recommendation: Revenue growth has declined primarily because of a slowdown in the generic product segment driven by capacity constraints and intensifying competition from overseas manufacturers

Silverado should raise luxury silverware pricing to $240 per unit, which maximizes luxury revenue at $36M and generates ~17% incremental growth, but this alone will not restore peak growth rates of ~26%

To fully restore growth, Silverado should pursue a combination of strategies: introduce a middle-tier product line, explore acquisitions with overseas capacity, and invest in expanding distribution channels
risks: The price elasticity data may be inaccurate, making the $240 price point risky
The cost of additional manufacturing capacity for generic output may not be economical
Saturation of the generic market could compress generic margins further
Overall market growth for silverware may slow, putting additional pressure on Silverado's growth targets
next_steps: Conduct a market study to validate price elasticity and test $240 price point with a pilot segment
Evaluate acquisition targets with overseas manufacturing capabilities
Develop business case for a middle-tier product line to capture the price gap between generic and luxury segments
Identify and establish new distribution partnerships in underserved channels
